assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Aarti Industries (consolidated, ₹ crore, revenue NET of GST as in the audited P&L and Screener; the company's headline 'revenue' of ₹9,018 cr for FY26 includes ₹732 cr of GST). One reportable segment (Ind AS 108), so revenue grows at a single rate and the EBITDA margin is a driver; energy / non-energy and value-chain volumes are tracked as KPIs. Net debt company: treasury yield is nil, interest is an explicit line. Valued on Sep-28E EV/EBITDA (primary), with P/E and DCF cross-checks.
assumptions._revenueWhy: FY27: Q1 net revenue +43% YoY, 'primarily driven by higher input prices passed on to customers' after the West Asia conflict lifted benzene, aniline, sulphur and methanol prices; volumes fell 12% QoQ. CRISIL (29-Sep-2026) expects >15% growth in FY27; PL 9,878 cr (+19%), ICICI Direct 9,688 cr (+17%). We use +18%: full-year fuel-additive capacity of 360 kT (vs 238 kT produced in FY26), DCB debottlenecking, the $150 mn agro contract, partly offset by softer prices in H2 and the winter dip in fuel additives. FY28: volumes +10-12% (Zone IV blocks, MPP, PEDA, Augene supplies) but input prices assumed to ease, so revenue +8%. FY29: +10% (CRISIL medium-term range 10-15%).
assumptions._marginWhy: FY26 14.1%. Q1FY27 16.0% included ₹50-60 cr of inventory and currency gains; CRISIL puts the underlying margin at ~14%. FY27 14.3% (Q1 actual plus ~14% for Q2-Q4, with the usual winter softness in fuel additives). FY28-29 15.0-15.5% as Zone IV and the NCB chain (China's export-VAT rebate removal) add margin and cost savings of ₹150-200 cr accrue; still below management's 14-15%-margin path to ₹1,800-2,200 cr of FY28 EBITDA, which we think will be met a year late at the low end (Aarti missed its first FY24 EBITDA target by ~29% and its FY25 target by ~41%).
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27: management ₹700-800 cr (₹180 cr spent in Q1): Zone IV completion, the 15-year backward-integration project (₹200-250 cr over two years) and ~₹150 cr maintenance. FY28-29: CRISIL expects ₹200-250 cr a year; we use ₹300-350 cr because the backward-integration project spills into FY28 and Aarti's capex has repeatedly come in above early guidance (FY26: ~₹1,000 cr guided, ₹1,125 cr spent).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹474 cr = 5.5% of average gross block (₹8,680 cr). Zone IV (~₹2,030 cr of capital work in progress at Mar-26) is capitalised during FY27; the engine adds only capex to the gross block and holds CWIP flat, so we use 6.0% on that smaller base to land depreciation at ~₹560-610 cr, in line with the CFO's FY28 bridge of ₹580-620 cr (May-2025 call).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Aarti carries net debt (~₹4,300 cr at Mar-26), so no treasury income is modelled; interest is an explicit line.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-operating income ₹5-20 cr a year (FY25 ₹17.5 cr, FY26 ₹4.9 cr before exceptional items) plus, from FY28, a small share of profit from the 50:50 Augene JV (equity-accounted; steady-state JV revenue guided at ₹300-400 cr).
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 finance cost ₹340 cr included ₹64 cr of exchange losses on foreign-currency loans; interest proper was ₹254 cr. Q1FY27 ₹83 cr as working-capital debt rose with input prices. FY27 ₹330 cr; FY28-29 lower as capex falls and debt is repaid (scheduled repayments ₹248-350 cr a year per CRISIL). CFO's FY28 bridge assumed ~₹250-270 cr at ₹1,800 cr EBITDA; we keep more debt because our EBITDA is lower.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective tax was −15% (tax credit: income-tax depreciation on new capacity, MAT credit and deferred tax assets on tax losses). Q1FY27 14%. Management guides 10-15% for FY27 and 9-15% thereafter while Zone IV tax depreciation lasts. We use 14% / 15% / 18%: the DCF applies the FY29 rate to all later years, so we lift FY29 towards the normal ~25% rate.
assumptions._payoutWhy: DPS ₹1 in FY24-FY26 (~9% of FY26 EPS); no change expected while net debt is above the company's 2.5x target.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts free cash flow at one rate (cost of equity = WACC). Aarti has debt, so we enter a WACC: cost of equity ~13.1% (beta 1.1) weighted ~78%, post-tax cost of debt ~6.5% weighted ~22% (net debt ~₹4,300 cr vs market value ~₹17,300 cr) = ~11.6%, which is what beta 0.85 produces. The same rate rolls the value forward 6 months.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian specialty-chemical demand grows with nominal GDP; 5.5% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% (FY29E) to 8% by year 15: volumes from new chemistry and fuel additives, little pricing power.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades to 5% of revenue, above maintenance, because Aarti has historically reinvested heavily; depreciation 4.5% of revenue.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Zone IV ramps on time from FY28, fuel additives run at full 360 kT with the Middle East reopening, and China's anti-involution keeps NCB margins firm: FY28 EBITDA reaches ~₹1,800 cr, the low end of guidance.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Crude-linked input prices fall and reverse the Q1 inventory gains, gasoline-naphtha cracks collapse (fuel-additive demand falls), Zone IV slips again and Chinese pricing pressure returns: EBITDA stays near ₹1,200-1,300 cr and net debt does not fall.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: The street is split between EV/EBITDA (ICICI Direct 14x FY28E) and P/E (PL 28x FY28E). We use EV/EBITDA because net debt is 3.6x EBITDA, the tax rate is temporarily 10-15% and depreciation on not-yet-earning assets depresses EPS: EBITDA less net debt captures all three. 12x = the stock's ~16x one-year-forward median since Apr-2023, less the ~31% sector de-rating (peer median vs post-2023 medians), plus ~1x for faster EBITDA growth as new capacity ramps up; no premium while ROCE (~7%) is below the cost of capital.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: The other half of the street (PL 28x FY28E EPS). 25x on Sep-28E: the stock's ~32x forward P/E median since Apr-2025 less part of the sector de-rating; lower than PL's 28x because our EPS is a year further out and taxed at only 15-18%.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at ~11.6% WACC, terminal growth 5.5%, less net debt.

cover.headline: A scale leader in benzene chemistry with a decade of capex still waiting to earn
cover.lead: Aarti Industries is India's largest maker of benzene-based intermediates (nitrochlorobenzenes, dichlorobenzenes, nitrotoluenes and their derivatives) and, since FY24, a large exporter of a gasoline octane booster (MMA), now 38-43% of revenue. It has spent ~₹7,640 cr on capex over FY21-26, yet FY26 EBITDA of ₹1,168 cr was only 19% above FY21, ROCE is ~7% and net debt has risen to ~₹4,300 cr (3.6x EBITDA). Management targets ₹1,800-2,200 cr of EBITDA in FY28; it missed its first FY24 and FY25 targets by 29% and 41%. We forecast ₹1,584 cr for FY28 and reach the low end a year late. The street is split between **EV/EBITDA** and P/E; we use **12x Sep-28E EV/EBITDA (₹1,692 cr), less ~₹3,246 cr of net debt**, which gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** P/E (₹476) and DCF (₹431) cross-checks agree. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}: the leverage makes the range wide.

arguments.p: Aarti is #1 globally in DCB and has 25-40% global share across its benzene products (CRISIL), with no customer above 10% of revenue. But Chinese supply sets prices: gross margin fell from 42% (FY23) to 34% (9MFY26), and FY26 realisations fell 25% while volumes rose 39%. China's export-VAT rebate removal (Apr-2026) has helped the NCB chain; PDA remains structurally weak.

arguments.h: Fuel additives: the growth engine is also the risk
arguments.p: MMA output rose from 23 kT (FY22) to 238 kT (FY26) and capacity reached 360 kT in Jul-2026. It carries a thin, crack-linked margin, faces 2-3 Indian and 2-3 Chinese competitors, and lost its Middle East market (~15% of company revenue to 2%) in Q1FY27. Volumes are seasonal (weak Oct-Dec).

arguments.h: Guidance has been unreliable; FY28 depends on Zone IV
arguments.p: FY25 EBITDA guidance started at ~₹1,700 cr and ended at ₹997 cr. Zone IV (₹1,600-1,800 cr, originally due FY25-26) is now commissioning in phases with a two-quarter delay, and none of the new projects has take-or-pay contracts. Q1FY27's record ₹382 cr EBITDA included ₹50-60 cr of inventory and currency gains.

At ₹475.7 the stock trades at 13.2x our FY28E EV/EBITDA and 28.5x FY28E EPS, 12% below its 52-week high. Our 12x Sep-28E multiple sits below its ~16x forward median since 2023 because the whole sector has de-rated ~31% and Aarti's returns are below its cost of capital. Upside needs EBITDA delivery, not a re-rating.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (late Oct / early Nov-2026): do volumes recover, and how much of Q1's inventory gain reverses as crude-linked prices ease?
Zone IV: commissioning of the five chemistry blocks in H2FY27 and customer re-qualification of commercial batches.
Fuel additives: utilisation of the 360 kT capacity, reopening of the Middle East, and the winter dip in gasoline cracks.
Net debt: management's internal target to cut net debt in FY27; CRISIL (AA/Negative) downgrade trigger at gross debt/EBITDA above 3.6x.
Management transition: Suyog Kotecha as MD from 1-Oct-2026, promoter executives move to non-executive roles.

sections.title: What Aarti does: turns benzene and toluene into 100+ intermediates, and sells an octane booster

blocks.p: Aarti Industries was founded in 1984 by first-generation technocrats of the Gogri family. It buys benzene (from Indian refiners), toluene, chlorine, nitric acid and sulphur, and runs them through chlorination, nitration, hydrogenation and ethylation to make more than 100 intermediates. These go into agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals (paracetamol starts from Aarti's PNCB), dyes and pigments, polymers and, since FY24, gasoline: the fuel-additive (energy) business makes MMA (monomethyl aniline) from imported aniline and sells it to refiners and blenders as an octane booster. It has 16 plants in Gujarat and Maharashtra, 5,800+ employees and 1,100+ customers in 60+ countries; no customer is 10% of revenue. The pharma business was demerged into Aarti Pharmalabs in 2022.

**A note on numbers.** Aarti's presentations quote revenue *including* GST: ₹9,018 cr for FY26 and ₹2,627 cr for Q1FY27. The audited net figures, used throughout this report and in our model, are ₹8,286 cr and ₹2,387 cr. The company reports a single business segment; end-use shares and volumes come from its presentations.

sections.title: Industry: Chinese overcapacity set the price for three years; policy has started to help

blocks.p: India's chemical industry is estimated at USD 155-165 bn and expected to reach USD 230-255 bn by 2030 (~8-9% a year), against 3-4% global growth (Aarti's FY26 annual report, citing industry sources). The opportunity is real: global customers want suppliers outside China, and India is the obvious alternative. But since 2022 Chinese capacity additions have flooded commodity and intermediate chemicals, and prices, not demand, have been the problem. Aarti's gross margin fell from 42% in FY23 to 34% in 9MFY26 against a ~45% decadal average (India Ratings), and its blended realisations fell 25% in FY26 even as volumes rose 39% (CRISIL).

sections.title: Non-energy chemistry: volumes up 15-70% since FY23, but each chain has its own problem

blocks.p: The non-energy business is Aarti's core: NCB, DCB, hydrogenation, PDA, nitrotoluene, ethylation and sulphuric-acid derivatives, sold to agro (18% of revenue), polymers (11-14%), dyes and pigments (11-15%) and pharma (10-14%). Volumes have grown well: FY26 output of NCB was 92.7 kT (+19% vs FY23), DCB 96.5 kT (+15%), NT 37.0 kT (+55%) and ethylation 20.5 kT (+72%). Most chains ran at 80-86% of capacity in FY26. The problem is margin: management concedes agro margins "remain under pressure", PDA is structurally weak because of a technology disadvantage, and NT margins have been depressed by an isomer imbalance. The bright spot is NCB, where China's removal of export VAT rebates (Apr-2026) lifted prices and margins.

sections.title: The energy business: 43% of revenue, a commodity spread and a single region shut

blocks.p: Aarti's "energy" business sells MMA (monomethyl aniline), an octane booster that refiners and blenders add to gasoline at under 1-2%. It is not methyl methacrylate and not fuel trading. Aarti makes MMA from imported aniline (mostly from China), so its spread depends on aniline prices on one side and the gasoline-naphtha crack (how much more gasoline is worth than naphtha) on the other. The business was ~15% of revenue in FY22-23; a 4-year ₹6,000 cr+ contract (Jan-2024) with a multinational conglomerate turned it into the growth engine: production rose from 37.8 kT (FY23) to 237.6 kT (FY26), energy revenue rose 36% to ₹3,563 cr in FY26 (CRISIL), and capacity reached 360 kT in Jul-2026.

sections.title: FY28 target of ₹1,800-2,200 cr EBITDA rests on projects that have slipped before

blocks.p: Management's FY28 bridge (from FY25 EBITDA of ~₹1,016 cr) adds ₹150-200 cr of cost savings (largely done), ₹350-550 cr from volume and margin ramp-up of existing assets (MMA, DCB, NCB, ethylation, NT) and ₹300-450 cr from new capex (Zone IV, MPP, PEDA, the Augene JV). Zone IV is a ₹1,600-1,800 cr greenfield site at Jhagadia designed around chlorotoluene and now built as five flexible chemistry blocks plus a multipurpose plant. blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Aarti has a **scale and integration advantage** in benzene chemistry (largest Indian producer, global top-3/top-4 positions) and **sticky customer relationships** (long-term contracts, a repeat contract from a global major, no customer above 10%). That is a real moat for *winning volume*. It is **not** a moat for *earning returns*: Chinese producers set the price in most of its chains, the energy business is a spread business, and ROCE has been ~7% for three years. A moat that does not show up in returns deserves a market multiple, not a premium.

sections.title: Quarters: a record Q1FY27, but inflated by prices, inventory and currency gains

blocks.p: Quarterly revenue has risen from ₹1,675 cr in Q1FY26 to ₹2,387 cr in Q1FY27 (+43%), and EBITDA from ₹212 cr to ₹382 cr. Read the Q1FY27 number carefully: management says revenue growth was "primarily driven by higher input prices passed on to customers" after the West Asia conflict lifted benzene, sulphur, methanol and aniline prices; volumes actually fell 12% from Q4FY26 (energy −17%, non-energy −7%). EBITDA was helped by ₹50-60 cr of inventory and currency gains (CEO estimate), so the underlying run-rate was roughly ₹320-330 cr, close to Q4FY26. Fuel additives (the energy business) are also seasonal: demand softens from late October to December as gasoline cracks weaken in winter.

sections.title: Revenue up 84% since FY21, EBITDA up only 19%: a decade of capex has not yet paid

blocks.p: Aarti's net revenue rose from ₹4,506 cr in FY21 to ₹8,286 cr in FY26 (13% a year), helped by new capacity and the fuel-additive (MMA) business. EBITDA did not follow: it peaked at ₹1,720 cr in FY22 (a year flattered by a one-off contract-termination receipt and by the pharma business, demerged in 2022), fell to ₹978 cr in FY24 and recovered only to ₹1,168 cr in FY26, just 19% above FY21. The EBITDA margin halved from 28% in FY22 to 14% in FY26 as Chinese oversupply cut prices across benzene-based chemicals and the fastest-growing product (MMA) carried a thin margin. Meanwhile depreciation and interest more than doubled, so net profit fell from ₹535 cr in FY21 to ₹419 cr in FY26.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but tax credits, inventory gains and FX make profit noisy

bullets: **Gross vs net revenue.** The headline ₹9,018 cr FY26 revenue includes ₹732 cr of GST; the audited net figure is ₹8,286 cr. Margins quoted by the company on the gross figure (13.0%) look lower than on the net (14.1%).

**Tax credits.** FY26 profit benefited from a tax *credit* (effective rate −15%): tax depreciation on new plants wiped out normal tax, MAT paid (₹64 cr) was booked as a MAT-credit asset, and deferred-tax assets on tax losses (₹324 cr) exceeded the deferred-tax liability (₹270 cr). Management guides 9-15% while Zone IV tax depreciation lasts; at a normal ~25% rate FY26 profit would have been ~₹270 cr, not ₹419 cr.

**Inventory and currency gains.** Q1FY27 EBITDA of ₹382 cr included ₹50-60 cr of inventory and FX gains (CEO, CRISIL). FX on trade is in EBITDA; FX on loans is in finance cost (₹64 cr loss in FY26, incl. ₹39 cr in Q4). When crude-linked prices fall, these gains reverse.
**Exceptional items.** FY26 included +₹28.5 cr of interest on tax refunds and −₹15.4 cr for the new labour codes.

**Working capital.** Receivables rose from ₹786 cr to ₹1,403 cr in FY26 (longer US voyages, revenue on delivery), operating cash flow fell from ₹1,238 cr to ₹781 cr, and ₹246 cr of supplier-finance arrangements sit inside payables. Working capital rose again in Q1FY27.
**Contract income.** Shortfall fees from customers (₹24 cr FY26, ₹72 cr FY25) are booked as operating revenue; FY22 included a ₹631 cr termination fee.
**Related parties.** Sales to promoter-linked Valiant Organics ₹273 cr; transport services from Kalpesh Roadlines ₹170 cr (a related party from Apr-2025); CSR of ₹12 cr to promoter-linked trusts.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** The audit by Gokhale & Sathe is unqualified, with revenue cut-off and inventory as key audit matters. We see no sign of manipulation, but reported profit is flattered by a below-normal tax rate and noisy with inventory and FX swings, and cash conversion weakened in FY26 (CFO/EBITDA 67% vs 124% in FY25).

sections.title: Net debt has risen to ~₹4,200 cr (3.6x EBITDA) after six years of negative free cash flow

blocks.p: Aarti has funded its capex mostly with debt. Over FY21-26 it generated ₹5,940 cr of operating cash flow but spent ₹7,640 cr on capex, and free cash flow was negative in every year (−₹340 cr in FY26). Net debt rose from ₹2,381 cr in FY21 to ₹4,226 cr in FY26 (company: ~₹4,300 cr), or 3.6x EBITDA, against management's own target of below 2.5x. The FY26 balance sheet also shows ₹2,030 cr of capital work in progress, mostly the ~₹1,800 cr Zone IV project that is not yet earning. In Q1FY27 working capital rose again with input prices and exports, so debt and finance costs went up. Receivable days jumped from 39 to 62 in FY26 as exports to the US (2-3 month voyages, revenue booked on delivery) grew.

blocks.p: The street is split. ICICI Direct values Aarti on **EV/EBITDA** (14x FY28E EBITDA); Prabhudas Lilladher on **P/E** (28x FY28E EPS); Emkay (2024-25) used P/E. Management and both rating agencies also frame the story in EBITDA and debt/EBITDA. We apply the multiple to Sep-28E (half FY28E, half FY29E) EBITDA and deduct net debt at the same date. assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Aarti Industries (consolidated, ₹ crore, revenue NET of GST as in the audited P&L and Screener; the company's headline 'revenue' of ₹9,018 cr for FY26 includes ₹732 cr of GST). One reportable segment (Ind AS 108), so revenue grows at a single rate and the EBITDA margin is a driver; energy / non-energy and value-chain volumes are tracked as KPIs. Net debt company: treasury yield is nil, interest is an explicit line. Valued on Sep-28E EV/EBITDA (primary), with P/E and DCF cross-checks.
assumptions._revenueWhy: FY27: Q1 net revenue +43% YoY, 'primarily driven by higher input prices passed on to customers' after the West Asia conflict lifted benzene, aniline, sulphur and methanol prices; volumes fell 12% QoQ. CRISIL (29-Sep-2026) expects >15% growth in FY27; PL 9,878 cr (+19%), ICICI Direct 9,688 cr (+17%). We use +18%: full-year fuel-additive capacity of 360 kT (vs 238 kT produced in FY26), DCB debottlenecking, the $150 mn agro contract, partly offset by softer prices in H2 and the winter dip in fuel additives. FY28: volumes +10-12% (Zone IV blocks, MPP, PEDA, Augene supplies) but input prices assumed to ease, so revenue +8%. FY29: +10% (CRISIL medium-term range 10-15%).
assumptions._marginWhy: FY26 14.1%. Q1FY27 16.0% included ₹50-60 cr of inventory and currency gains; CRISIL puts the underlying margin at ~14%. FY27 14.3% (Q1 actual plus ~14% for Q2-Q4, with the usual winter softness in fuel additives). FY28-29 15.0-15.5% as Zone IV and the NCB chain (China's export-VAT rebate removal) add margin and cost savings of ₹150-200 cr accrue; still below management's 14-15%-margin path to ₹1,800-2,200 cr of FY28 EBITDA, which we think will be met a year late at the low end (Aarti missed its first FY24 EBITDA target by ~29% and its FY25 target by ~41%).
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27: management ₹700-800 cr (₹180 cr spent in Q1): Zone IV completion, the 15-year backward-integration project (₹200-250 cr over two years) and ~₹150 cr maintenance. FY28-29: CRISIL expects ₹200-250 cr a year; we use ₹300-350 cr because the backward-integration project spills into FY28 and Aarti's capex has repeatedly come in above early guidance (FY26: ~₹1,000 cr guided, ₹1,125 cr spent).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹474 cr = 5.5% of average gross block (₹8,680 cr). Zone IV (~₹2,030 cr of capital work in progress at Mar-26) is capitalised during FY27; the engine adds only capex to the gross block and holds CWIP flat, so we use 6.0% on that smaller base to land depreciation at ~₹560-610 cr, in line with the CFO's FY28 bridge of ₹580-620 cr (May-2025 call).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Aarti carries net debt (~₹4,300 cr at Mar-26), so no treasury income is modelled; interest is an explicit line.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-operating income ₹5-20 cr a year (FY25 ₹17.5 cr, FY26 ₹4.9 cr before exceptional items) plus, from FY28, a small share of profit from the 50:50 Augene JV (equity-accounted; steady-state JV revenue guided at ₹300-400 cr).
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 finance cost ₹340 cr included ₹64 cr of exchange losses on foreign-currency loans; interest proper was ₹254 cr. Q1FY27 ₹83 cr as working-capital debt rose with input prices. FY27 ₹330 cr; FY28-29 lower as capex falls and debt is repaid (scheduled repayments ₹248-350 cr a year per CRISIL). CFO's FY28 bridge assumed ~₹250-270 cr at ₹1,800 cr EBITDA; we keep more debt because our EBITDA is lower.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective tax was −15% (tax credit: income-tax depreciation on new capacity, MAT credit and deferred tax assets on tax losses). Q1FY27 14%. Management guides 10-15% for FY27 and 9-15% thereafter while Zone IV tax depreciation lasts. We use 14% / 15% / 18%: the DCF applies the FY29 rate to all later years, so we lift FY29 towards the normal ~25% rate.
assumptions._payoutWhy: DPS ₹1 in FY24-FY26 (~9% of FY26 EPS); no change expected while net debt is above the company's 2.5x target.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts free cash flow at one rate (cost of equity = WACC). Aarti has debt, so we enter a WACC: cost of equity ~13.1% (beta 1.1) weighted ~78%, post-tax cost of debt ~6.5% weighted ~22% (net debt ~₹4,300 cr vs market value ~₹17,300 cr) = ~11.6%, which is what beta 0.85 produces. The same rate rolls the value forward 6 months.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian specialty-chemical demand grows with nominal GDP; 5.5% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% (FY29E) to 8% by year 15: volumes from new chemistry and fuel additives, little pricing power.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades to 5% of revenue, above maintenance, because Aarti has historically reinvested heavily; depreciation 4.5% of revenue.

We use EV/EBITDA because net debt is 3.6x EBITDA, the tax rate is temporarily 10-15% and depreciation on not-yet-earning assets depresses EPS: EBITDA less net debt captures all three. 12x = the stock's ~16x one-year-forward median since Apr-2023, less the ~31% sector de-rating (peer median vs post-2023 medians), plus ~1x for faster EBITDA growth as new capacity ramps up; no premium while ROCE (~7%) is below the cost of capital.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: The other half of the street (PL 28x FY28E EPS). 25x on Sep-28E: the stock's ~32x forward P/E median since Apr-2025 less part of the sector de-rating; lower than PL's 28x because our EPS is a year further out and taxed at only 15-18%.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at ~11.6% WACC, terminal growth 5.5%, less net debt.
